# MDL406 · `invalid-regex`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

A regular-expression option's value does not compile.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | options |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Design references | F4 |

## Why

mydumper compiles options such as `regex` with PCRE2 and aborts at startup when the expression is invalid. mydumper-lint checks it with a PCRE-like engine (regexp2), so a few PCRE-only constructs may be reported by mistake: hence a warning. The value is used as written, quotes included (F4).

## Example

With mydumper v0.19.3-3:

❌ Before:

```ini
[mydumper]
regex=^(db1|db2\.
```

```text
2:7-2:18 warning MDL406[invalid-regex] `regex` is not a valid regular expression: error parsing regexp: missing closing ) in `^(db1|db2\.`
  = mydumper aborts when it compiles the expression ("Regular expression fail").
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL406: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL406` on the line above it.
